reviews.review:
[Incoming Transmission…]

This is Colonial Marine unit [REDACTED] aboard the Katanga. We are knee-deep in xenomorphs and running low on ammo. The halls are crawling, the walls are alive, and every shadow has teeth. We can’t hold out much longer.

If you’re reading this, we need reinforcements. Grab your pulse rifle, load up your smartgun, and get your squad together. The only way I’m making it out of here is if you buy Aliens: Fireteam Elite and drop in to cover my six. Don’t leave a Marine behind. Transmission ends.

I didn't like it too much. I played it some time after Colonial Marines and expected something of that magnitude. But it's just... bland. The marine ship feels dead, een though there are some marines on board there is simply no interaction whatsoever. If you do have a possibility to speak with anybody, devs didn't even bother with lip syncing. It's non-existent. Stupid marine just stares at you blankly like an android and doesn;t even move his mouth during speaking. I also don't like there are zero interactions at all durnig the missions - seriously, would that hurt to create three or four marines who actually have any kind of personality, so that you are not being stuck with "Alpha" and "Beta" mechs....? Plot is actually non-existent and you are doing everything the same way in each mission - go find something, pull a lever, hit a button, defeat a wave, rince, repeat.

reviews.review:
Actually pretty fun, you can play it as single player game and probably still enjoy it, the bots are absolutely fine on the first 2 difficulty modes.

I feel like if it had a little more variation, it could've kept things fresh for a lot more time. 
I absolutely would not mind if the maps/missions were shorter and instead we had a few random 'segments', that changed things a little every time you play, like paths blocked, random events, etc.
